messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Compute roster validation for contract close — Aerodyne Systems

Team,

Aerodyne's legal/commercial team signaled a likely close by the end of the month (deal id DEAL-2247). Before we commit commercial terms we need a quick validation of available dedicated capacity and a short provisional hold on the fleet so we don't get scoped out during procurement. High level ask from the AE/SE:

- Required baseline: 8x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs sustained for the first 6 months, with ability to burst to 12 for short training/bench runs.
- Preferred placement: single dedicated pool in us-west with node isolation (no multi-tenant co-scheduling).
- SLO guidance: 99.9% availability, 60ms generate p50 for 2k token seq on the model family they plan to serve.

I've attached the capacity ask workbook (capacity_ask_aerodyne.xlsx) with numbers AE put together. Please take a look and confirm: 1) we have spare capacity in the target pool for the committed window; 2) whether we can set a soft escrow/hold (non-billing) for 30–45 days until contract signature; 3) any suggested mitigations if capacity is tight (model shard/quantization alternatives, autoscale windows, or cross-region fallback).

Can you reply with a short yes/no + recommended next step by EOD tomorrow? If yes, Laura — can you draft the internal hold ticket so we can show logistics to the customer?

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_ask_aerodyne.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compute roster validation for contract close — Aerodyne Systems

Marcus / team —

Quick read on capacity_ask_aerodyne.xlsx. TL;DR: we can cover the baseline with a soft hold, but there are two caveats and a recommended plan: 

Caveats:
- Us-west pool current spare: ~10 A100-80GB-equivalents in the dedicated pool that meet isolation constraints. After existing commitments we'd be at ~2 spare if we don't place a hold.
- Burst capacity to 12 is possible but would require temporary reallocation from the shared spare (risk: short-term latency variance).

Recommendation (safe path):
1) Place a provisional non-billing hold on 8 units for 45 days to secure runway while procurement closes. Label the hold as DEAL-2247-provisional so ops can track.
2) Configure canary autoscale with a 10% reserved buffer for the first 30 days and allow scheduled burst windows for benchmark jobs (we can gate bursts with a temporary quota).
3) If we see another late-stage request in the next 2 weeks, start shifting lower-priority dedicated commitments to threshold pools flagged as overflow (we have 6 convertible nodes in us-west).

Operational steps I can take once Laura creates the ticket: create the hold in the capacity registry, tag the nodes with "deal:DEAL-2247" and set burst policy flags. I'll also update the fleet-map (attached) to show exactly which racks/nodes are being earmarked — see roster_map_03.png.

Note: the hold is reversible if we get pushback from infra; we should still surface this to infra leads since provisioning changes may require notices.

Rishi
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

Attachments: roster_map_03.png (PNG map of node allocation)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: capacity-ops@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compute roster validation for contract close — Aerodyne Systems

Marcus / Rishi —

Thanks for the details. I created internal ticket CAP-HOLD-9817 and set the provisional hold parameters: 8 units, 45 days, label DEAL-2247-provisional, pool=us-west-dedicated-1. The ticket includes a rollback window and owner (me). I've also notified infra leads (cc'd capacity-ops) about the potential burst window and the risk notes you called out.

What I did: 
- Ticket CAP-HOLD-9817 created and linked to DEAL-2247 in our capacity tracker (https://infra.redwood.com/capacity/CAP-HOLD-9817).
- Nodes tentatively reserved: racks r12-r13, nodes r12n[01-04], r13n[01-04] (matching Rishi's map).
- Burst policy: 12-unit burst allowed for scheduled benchmark jobs between 0100-0500 PST; will require infra approval if used outside those windows.

Next steps for the sales thread: Marcus, when you talk to procurement please share the CAP-HOLD-9817 reference and the attached short MOP (deal_mop.pdf) so they understand this is provisional and non-billing until signing. I'll keep the ticket open and post status updates every 48 hours.

Laura Bennett
Capacity Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: deal_mop.pdf (ops playbook, 2 pages)

Sanjay —

Forwarding the internal confirmation for the compute runway you requested. Short summary for your procurement team: 

- We have placed a provisional (non-billing) hold for 8 GPU units in our us-west dedicated pool for 45 days. Reference: CAP-HOLD-9817 / DEAL-2247-provisional.
- Burst capacity to 12 units is available under a scheduled window; we recommend using the benchmark window during off-peak hours to avoid latency impact.
- This hold is reversible and will not incur charges until the contract is signed; we do however ask that Aerodyne move procurement through the standard PO/signature process in the next 30 days to avoid rollback.

Attached are the internal MOP and the capacity workbook we used to size the ask. Laura will update CAP-HOLD-9817 as things progress. If procurement wants a short 15–20 minute operational briefing (how holds work, burst rules, rollback), Laura and Rishi are available tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
